CVE-2017-3164.title: Server Side Request Forgery in Apache Solr, versions 1.3 until 7. ...
CVE-2017-3164.description: Server Side Request Forgery in Apache Solr, versions 1.3 until 7.6 (inclusive). Since the "shards" parameter does not have a corresponding whitelist mechanism, a remote attacker with access to the server could make Solr perform an HTTP GET request to any reachable URL.

CVE-2019-17558.title: Apache Solr 5.0.0 to Apache Solr 8.3.1 are vulnerable to a Remote ...
CVE-2019-17558.description: Apache Solr 5.0.0 to Apache Solr 8.3.1 are vulnerable to a Remote Code Execution through the VelocityResponseWriter. A Velocity template can be provided through Velocity templates in a configset `velocity/` directory or as a parameter. A user defined configset could contain renderable, potentially malicious, templates. Parameter provided templates are disabled by default, but can be enabled by setting `params.resource.loader.enabled` by defining a response writer with that setting set to `true`. Defining a response writer requires configuration API access. Solr 8.4 removed the params resource loader entirely, and only enables the configset-provided template rendering when the configset is `trusted` (has been uploaded by an authenticated user).

CVE-2026-53672.title: A bug related to the Zookeeper HTTP endpoints in Apache Solr allo ...
CVE-2026-53672.description:
A bug related to the Zookeeper HTTP endpoints in Apache Solr allows an authenticated attacker with zk-read permission to read /security.json, bypassing the security-read authorization check. This may cause unauthorized read of credential hashes and authorization configuration.

For this attack to be successful, the following must be true
  *  The system is secured with Solr's Basic Auth plugin
  *  The attacker has gained direct network access to the Solr cluster
  *  The attacker has obtained credentials for a user account with zk-read permission (which is recommended assigned to trusted admins only)


Users are recommended to upgrade to 9.11.0, 10.1.0 or a newer release.
Users who cannot upgrade immediately are recommended to assign the zk-read permission only to users who they entrust reading security.json.

CVE-2026-86312.title: Under some configurations a request to the ping endpoint could ca ...
CVE-2026-86312.description:
Under some configurations a request to the ping endpoint could carry out more than a simple health check. In deployments that rely on Solr's rule-based authorization, a client granted only the low-privilege health permission could thereby trigger behavior that should require higher privileges; where the shipped security.json template leaves the health permission unauthenticated, no credentials are required at all. 


This issue affects Apache Solr from 9.0.0 through the releases preceding the fixed versions. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 9.11.0 or 10.1.0, which resolve the issue.




You are affected if you run an affected version and allow the /admin/ping endpoint to be reached with only the health permission. This includes the default sample security configuration installed by the bin/solr CLI, where that endpoint is unauthenticated.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should restrict access to the /admin/ping endpoint in their authorization configuration — for example by requiring a trusted role for that path — and ensure Solr is not reachable from untrusted clients or networks, as recommended for all Solr deployments.
